clue.text: It's beginning to coagulate with very warm temperature?

definitions.text: It's beginning to coagulate with very warm temperature?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of the following word is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of coagulate
very warm means hot
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a thing starts to set when the weather gets very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as a loose description: a chott is a North African salt lake that dries out in the heat, leaving its salt to set like a crust.
explanation.definitionFit: A chott is a shallow saline lake in North Africa which evaporates in the hot season, so the heat makes it solidify into salt.

clue.text: Prezzie time, half of microbrewery disposed of

indicators.note: taking only half of a word means dropping the other half of its letters
things disposed are arranged or set out afresh, so the kept letters are placed in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; only its first six letters stay

explanation.surface: Christmas is coming, and half the stock of a small brewery has been got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposed of' reads as 'got rid of', but here it means arranged. 'Prezzie' is British slang for a present, and Crimbo is British slang for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is the festival of giving presents, and Crimbo is its informal British nickname.

clue.text: Gardener accepting opposite points to poet at all events

definitions.note: 'to poet' marks the shortened poetic form

indicators.note: someone accepting something takes it in, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: a gardener who wields a hoe
west and east are opposite points of the compass

explanation.surface: A gardener puts up with a poet's contrary views, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: HOWE'ER is the contracted form of however found in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: However can mean in any case or nevertheless, which is the sense of at all events; poets elide it to keep the metre.

clue.text: Awfully hot and dry, I swallowed what moves up and down in the throat?

definitions.text: swallowed what moves up and down in the throat?

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a hot, dry throat gulps and feels something bob up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: The thyroid cartilage, the Adam's apple, rises and falls when you swallow; the question mark admits the description is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyroid cartilage forms the Adam's apple, the lump in the neck seen bobbing during a gulp.

clue.text: Doctor t-to encircle description of certain chromosomes

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a stammered 'to', taken letter for letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic stammers about having to surround something while describing chromosomes.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog's copy drops the stammer; without the printed 't-to' the fodder is a T short.
explanation.definitionFit: Telocentric is the term for chromosomes whose centromere lies at one end, so it is an adjective describing a certain kind of chromosome.

clue.text: Head-men stirring panic about palm tree

indicators.note: stirring something mixes it up, so these letters are scrambled
about means around, so the scrambled letters wrap round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be scrambled
the ita is a South American palm

explanation.surface: Leaders are causing alarm over a palm tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitani is the plural of capitano, an Italian word for a chief or captain, so head men.

clue.text: Ageless use of winch for measure of fish freshly landed

indicators.note: less means without, so the abbreviation for age is dropped

blocks.note: a crane is a winching machine for lifting
E is an abbreviation for age (era)

explanation.surface: A timeless use of a winch to hoist a catch of fish ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran is a measure, about 37.5 gallons, used for fresh herrings just landed.

clue.text: I'm promised shelf in gym

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held within it

blocks.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
a ledge is a shelf

explanation.surface: Someone has been guaranteed a shelf in the gymnasium.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the answer speaks of itself as the one who has been promised something.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledgee is the person to whom a pledge is given, the one who has been promised.

clue.text: Fliers tense with gremlins about, revealing weaknesses

indicators.note: about means around, so the mischievous sprites go round the rest

blocks.note: gremlins are mischievous imps
fliers are airmen
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Pilots are on edge because gremlins are in the aircraft, exposing faults.
explanation.walkthrough: Gremlins were the imps RAF airmen blamed for mechanical faults, so the surface is a neat wartime scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Impairments are damages or deficiencies, so they are weak points.

clue.text: Any old cart shifting barrels on top

indicators.note: shifting something moves it away, so it is taken off the word
on top points at the head of this down entry, where the removed letter sat

blocks.note: a barrow is a small cart
b. is an abbreviation for barrels

explanation.surface: A cart, any old one, is unloading the barrels piled on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Any old cart' reads as one phrase, but 'Any old' is the definition: 'old' marks an obsolete dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrow is an obsolete dialect form of ary, meaning any, so it is an old word for any.

clue.text: What'll emerge from combing formal dress with this yields thanks!

blocks.note: surface reading: the debris left in a comb

blocks.clueFragment: formal dress with this yields thanks!
blocks.note: setter's reading: 'this' is read as an instruction to strip certain letters from the evening suit, leaving a short word of gratitude

explanation.surface: Grooming leaves bits behind, and formal dress earns gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'no ILS': formal dress TAILS with no I, L or S is TA, British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Noils are the short fibres separated out when wool or silk is combed, so they are what combing produces as waste.

clue.text: One won't top bull that is getting tip of horn twice in rear of toreador

indicators.note: a tip is an end, so only the end letter of the word is used
getting means receiving, so the first piece takes the second inside it
the rear of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
the end letter of horn, taken two times
the final letter of toreador

explanation.surface: A bull is gored by a horn while a bullfighter tries to stay on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull is the bullseye of a target, not an animal; 'won't top' means scores less than.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery and darts the inner is the ring just outside the bullseye, so a shot there scores less than the bull.

clue.text: Old oxen, head of redpoll et al?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of redpoll
et al is Latin for and others

explanation.surface: Cattle are listed after a red-headed finch and the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: A redpoll is a finch, but it is also a breed of red cattle, which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: Rother is an archaic word for an ox or cow, so rothers are old-fashioned oxen.

clue.text: Space filler bridging gap in thinnish impromptu

indicators.note: the answer spans the gap between two words of the clue, straddling the space

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of thinnish into the start of impromptu

explanation.surface: A thin makeshift piece fills a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator itself describes the device: the answer bridges the space between the two words, just as the definition describes filling a space.
explanation.definitionFit: A shim is a thin wedge or strip slipped into a gap to make parts fit, so it fills a space.

clue.text: Press piece

blocks.note: first meaning: to smooth clothes with a heated appliance
second meaning: slang for a handgun

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press piece' suggests a newspaper article; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them flat, and in gangster slang both piece and iron mean a gun.

clue.text: Internet I consider with care, judging from hearsay

indicators.note: hearsay is what is heard, so the words are judged by their sound

blocks.note: to weigh something is to consider it carefully

explanation.surface: Someone says they treat the internet cautiously, going by what others say.
explanation.definitionFit: The i-way, short for information superhighway, is an old informal name for the internet.

clue.text: Man cutting loses fourth of fingers — this'll delay clotting

indicators.note: losing something means it goes, so a letter is removed
fourth picks out the letter in fourth position of the next word

blocks.note: he is a man, as a pronoun
a paring is a cutting, such as a nail clipping
the fourth letter of fingers

explanation.surface: A man slicing something loses part of his finger, and something is needed to stop the bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a wound that should clot; the answer does the opposite, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Heparin is an anticoagulant drug, a substance that slows the formation of blood clots.

clue.text: Altered 'zoom' in mobile? It may help STD

indicators.note: mobile means able to move, so the letters move around

blocks.note: all three words are fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A zoom feature has been changed on a mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altered' looks like the anagram signal and 'mobile' like a phone, but Altered is fodder and mobile is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Metronidazole is an antibiotic used to treat sexually transmitted infections such as trichomoniasis.

clue.text: Make fun of old medic diving into stream

indicators.note: diving into something puts you inside it

blocks.note: a beck is a northern English word for a stream
MO, medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: People jeer at an elderly doctor plunging into a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemock is an old literary word meaning to mock or ridicule.

clue.text: Joint stuffed with fish left as something to go in the soup

definitions.text: something to go in the soup

indicators.note: something stuffed with a filling has it packed inside

blocks.note: the knee is a joint
the id, or ide, is a freshwater fish
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A cut of meat filled with fish is left to go into the soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A kneidel is a matzo-meal dumpling served in Jewish chicken soup.

clue.text: Soak provided reverses for old-time incendiary

indicators.note: to reverse is to run backwards, so the joined pieces are read from end to start

blocks.note: a soak is a heavy drinker, a toper
provided means if

explanation.surface: A drunkard, given the chance, backtracks on a fire bomb of yesteryear.
explanation.definitionFit: A firepot was an earthen pot of combustibles hurled as a weapon in old warfare.

clue.text: Though not the first, customer's fine concerning the runs?

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: a customer is a client
an eric was a blood-fine paid for murder in old Irish law

explanation.surface: A shopper is told that, though not first in line, they have a penalty to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The runs' is slang for diarrhoea; 'fine' looks like an adjective but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lienteric is the adjective for lientery, a form of diarrhoea in which food passes undigested.

clue.text: Dad holding rule repositioned side-pieces

indicators.note: things repositioned are put in new places, so the letters are rearranged
holding means having inside, so the father wraps round the rest

blocks.note: pa is a word for dad
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A father moves the side panels around while keeping order.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleura is the plural of pleuron, the side plate of a segment in an insect or crustacean, hence side-pieces.

clue.text: First pair for Kevin leaving centre of square? That's Aussie leg-pulling

indicators.note: the first pair of a word is its opening two letters
leaving the centre means going out of the middle, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: Berkeley Square is a famous square in London's Mayfair
the opening two letters of Kevin

explanation.surface: A man named Kevin walks off from the middle of a square, and an Australian says he is joking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is only an example of the London square Berkeley Square, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang berley is groundbait, and by extension nonsense or humbug used to fool someone.

clue.text: MP shows little depth in this summary

indicators.note: the military officer's title is this word with a small depth sign shown in it, so removing that sign leaves the word

blocks.note: a redcap is a military policeman, so an MP
d is the abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A politician's précis is criticised for being shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: MP looks like a Member of Parliament, but it is a Military Policeman, nicknamed for the red cover on his cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap, short for recapitulation, is a brief restatement of the main points.

clue.text: Flamenco I've played? If me with this sort of castanet, no!

indicators.note: letters played like notes are performed in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken as written; joined with the answer it forms part of the fodder
taken as written; also part of the fodder alongside the answer

explanation.surface: A flamenco dancer asks whether they should perform with castanets, and answers no.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer together with 'If me' and 'no' uses the same letters as 'Flamenco I've'.
explanation.definitionFit: Claves are a pair of hardwood sticks clicked together in Latin music, a percussion instrument akin to castanets.

clue.text: Translator holds one up producing exact legal transcript

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside
in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: tr. is the abbreviation for translator
the word one, read upwards

explanation.surface: An interpreter raises a document and makes an exact copy for court.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the tenor of a document is an exact copy or transcript of it.

clue.text: Fair in due course repeated

blocks.note: so can mean then, in due course, as in 'and so to bed'
the same word again

explanation.surface: Something fair will come round again in time.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means middling or passable, which is one sense of fair.

clue.text: Poet's rival successfully has run in dash

indicators.note: to have something here is to hold it, so one letter sits inside

blocks.note: emule is Spenser's word for emulate, to rival successfully
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A poet's competitor wins after a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet is Spenser, whose archaic spellings Chambers lists.
explanation.definitionFit: An em rule is the long dash used in printing, as wide as the letter M.

clue.text: English left, unstable coterie, never getting in, requiring one to enthuse voters?

indicators.note: something unstable will not hold its shape, so the letters shift
getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written, to be scrambled
ne'er is the contracted form of never

explanation.surface: An unsteady left-wing English clique, never in power, needs a campaigner to rally voters.
explanation.definitionFit: An electioneerer is someone who campaigns to win votes, so a person who rouses the electorate.

clue.text: Talent, sine qua non for Carnoustie

indicators.note: a sine qua non is an essential element, something contained within the place name

blocks.note: the middle letters of Carnoustie

explanation.surface: Skill is essential for golf at Carnoustie.
explanation.walkthrough: Carnoustie is a famous Scottish links golf course, which is why talent sounds essential there.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is practical intelligence or know-how, close in sense to talent or ability.

clue.text: False rumours? One in a pack maybe

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a pack, for example, of playing cards
an means one

explanation.surface: Untrue stories come one at a time, perhaps from a whole pack of lies.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a baseless story or hoax spread as news.

clue.text: Collingwood catch? One in hoisted to leg, led astray

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
something gone astray has wandered away, so those letters are lost

blocks.note: in cricket a pull hits the ball to the leg side
a means one
taken as written; these letters go

explanation.surface: A cricketer takes a catch from a ball hoisted to the leg side, which went off course.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Collingwood is an England cricketer known for spectacular catches; a paul is also a ratchet catch (pawl). In cricket, the leg side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul is Collingwood's first name, and paul is a variant spelling of pawl, a pivoted catch that stops a ratchet slipping.

clue.text: Acknowledge what's spent in Macau on women

blocks.note: the avo is a coin of Macau, a hundredth of a pataca
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Someone admits what they splashed out on women in Macau's casinos.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to admit or declare openly, so to acknowledge.

clue.text: Our English takes in pull over in Scotland

indicators.note: taking something in means enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
to tow is to pull

explanation.surface: Our English driver hauls a car to the roadside north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull over' reads as a driving phrase, but 'over' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Outowre is a Scots form of outower, meaning over or across.

clue.text: Eponymous hero, person standing for art in things

indicators.note: standing for means replacing, so one piece takes the place of another

blocks.note: articles are things or items
taken as written; this is what is swapped out
per. is the dictionary abbreviation for person

explanation.surface: A title character stands in for art amid a collection of objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericles is the title character of Shakespeare's play Pericles, Prince of Tyre, so the hero who gives the play its name.

clue.text: A common street, look

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a ray is a look or glance of the eye

explanation.surface: Someone points out an ordinary road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like an adjective for the street, but it is a noun: a stray is common land, as at Harrogate's Stray in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray is a dialect word for an area of common grazing land, so a common.
